records.name: Philadelphia Chinatown Development Corp.
records.summary: The community development group for Chinatown. It builds affordable housing, offers housing counseling and help getting benefits, runs the Crane Community Center, and hosts events such as the Night Market. The City also names it a Neighborhood Advisory Committee, which links residents to City programs.
records.what_you_do: Volunteer at neighborhood events, join or use the programs at Crane Community Center, or ask the Neighborhood Advisory Committee about City help with housing, energy bills, jobs and youth programs.

schedule.text: Senior morning sports at Crane Community Center on Mondays, Wednesdays and Fridays, 10:30 am to 12:30 pm, for people 65 and older.

cost.text: Crane Community Center membership is $80 a year and gives 50 percent off community sessions. Senior morning sports cost $3 a session for people 65 and older, with no membership needed.

first_step.how: Join the PCDC newsletter and say you want to volunteer, or email info@chinatown-pcdc.org.
first_step.basis: The Get Involved page says volunteer requests go out to the newsletter list and gives an email and a phone line. Senior sports are open to anyone 65 and older for a small fee.
first_step.what_to_expect: Volunteer jobs are tied to PCDC events and are mostly one time. Senior morning sports run three mornings a week at Crane Community Center for $3 a session.
first_visit_tips: Call 215-922-6156 before you come, since the pages checked do not list office hours.
Check the events page for dates, because at least one summer event moved to a new day.
The PCDC office is at 301-305 North 9th Street. The Crane Community Center street address is not on the pages checked.

records.notes: The Teams meeting link and its passcode, which were in the City list text for the meeting place, were removed along with the alternate meeting address. NAC meeting times are not on the site. Phone changed to the main office line (215-922-6156). The City list number (215-922-2156) is the Crane Community Center line on the site. The site's general email is info@chinatown-pcdc.org; the City list contact email is kept. The Philly Pops at Crane story gives no event date. The Night Market is October 8, 2026, 6 to 10 pm, and sits in last_sign_of_life, not in schedule.

records.name: One Little Earth
records.summary: A nonprofit that makes and supports children's books and films about nature. It also pays for school film screenings.

cost.text: No fees are listed on the site.

records.notes: Judgment call for the owner. The group makes and supports children's books and films about nature for schools and libraries. Its site lists no volunteer roles, no memberships, no public events with dates, and no working newsletter sign-up: the sign-up link goes back to the homepage. The festival page describes the Philadelphia Environmental Film Festival in the past tense, with listed editions only up to 2022. Hidden as out of scope (no public way in). Tier 1 had it as publish. If the owner wants it listed, it would publish with newcomer rating 2 and a first step of watching the news page. Its only published email is a personal address, which was not recorded.

records.name: Philadelphia Freedom Band
records.summary: An LGBTQ+ community band with several ensembles, including concert and marching bands. It welcomes anyone who wants to play and shares its mission.
records.what_you_do: Play in one of the band's ensembles and take part in its concerts and Pride performances.

schedule.text: Rehearsal days and times were not listed on the band's website at the last check.

cost.text: Dues and fees were not stated on the pages checked in the first pass.

first_step.how: Use the contact link on the band's website to ask how to join.
first_step.basis: The band says anyone who wants to play and shares its mission can take part, and it lists a contact route. No audition or dues are described on the pages checked in the first pass.

records.notes: The band's website could not be read. The fetch tool refused both the bare and the www host because the certificate belongs to another hosting service (a TLS name mismatch), which is not a bot check. So this record is still tier 1: the join, rehearsal and dues facts are the first-pass ones. Status moved to active on the basis of the May 2026 Pride Bands Alliance listing, which the first pass recorded as the newest dated item; that conference appearance moved out of schedule.text. A single WebSearch turned up public descriptions of concert, marching and jazz ensembles, roughly 100 musicians, and free public concerts in spring and winter. None of that is recorded as fact because the snippets could not be checked against the band's own site. Retry the site in a later pass.

records.name: Philadelphia Rugby Football Club
aka: Philadelphia Womens Rugby Football Club Inc
records.summary: A rugby club founded in 1976 that began as a women's club and now welcomes players of any gender identity. It fields Division I and Division III 15s teams and a summer sevens program.
records.what_you_do: Train at Tuesday and Thursday evening practices, play 15s in the fall and spring or summer sevens, and work a few stadium game day shifts each season.

schedule.text: Practice on Tuesdays and Thursdays from about 7:30 pm at Scanlon Rec Center in Philadelphia. Weather or field problems can move a practice, and the club gives notice.

locations.label: Practice field
locations.address: Scanlon Rec Center, 1099 E Venango St, Philadelphia, PA 19134

cost.text: Returning 15s players pay $125 a season, and new players and students pay $100, with a $50 social option. USA Rugby registration adds $76.50 a year. Payment plans go through the treasurer.

requirements.gear: A mouth guard and cleats (soccer cleats are fine). Match days also need the club's black socks and plain black shorts.

first_step.how: Email recruiting@philadelphiarugby.org to say you want to join, since the site sends interested players there.
first_step.basis: The FAQ says no experience is needed and the club welcomes every skill level. The practice page sends interested players to a recruiting email. No beginner session or open practice is listed.
first_step.what_to_expect: Practices run about two hours on Tuesday and Thursday evenings, and the club trains players at all levels. Expect a season fee, a USA Rugby registration before your first match, and a few stadium shifts over the season.
first_visit_tips: Bring a mouth guard and cleats; soccer cleats are fine.
Ask the treasurer about a payment plan before you pay the full season fee.
Practice is at Scanlon Rec Center, 1099 E Venango St, Philadelphia, PA 19134.
Weather or field problems can move practice to another spot, and the club gives notice.

records.notes: The site uses two email domains: the recruiting and treasurer addresses are on philadelphiarugby.org, but some sevens links point to pwrfc.org. The record uses philadelphiarugby.org as displayed; the owner may want to confirm. The City list contact name 'Organization' was dropped because it is not a person. The pages read give no age or gender limits; the homepage says the club welcomes players of any gender identity. The last_sign_of_life comes from the 2026 summer sevens fees and June 13 payment date. Division I players work 3 to 6 stadium events a season and Division III players at least one. The practice page says practices are usually at Scanlon Rec Center, so the location is not fixed.

records.name: Philadelphia Women in Film and Television
records.summary: A nonprofit that supports and recognizes women working in film, TV, video and multimedia in the Philadelphia area. Members get networking and reduced prices on workshops, can join committees, and the group runs a grant for first-time female directors.
records.what_you_do: Pay yearly dues to become a member, join one of the group's committees, and take part in member events when they are listed. The events page lists no current events; its newest listings are from 2024.

cost.text: Individual membership is $75 a year, and student membership is $25 a year with a student ID. A $50 a year individual renewal rate is also listed. Corporate membership is $250 a year.

first_step.how: Pay the membership dues by PayPal or by check, wait for the registration form, then email it with your resume to membership@pwift.org.
first_step.basis: Membership needs dues and a registration form before you get to the member events, and the events list shows no current public events to try first.
first_step.what_to_expect: Individual membership is for people working in film, video or related media. Joining is a yearly payment, then a registration form and resume go to the membership team. Members get free admission to members-only events, reduced prices on special events and workshops, a bi-monthly newsletter, and access to a members' Facebook group.
first_visit_tips: Email info@pwift.org with questions before you pay, because the public events list is out of date.
Students need a valid student ID for the $25 rate, and the student tier is tied to schools in the Greater Philadelphia area.
The Palmer Enfield grant for first-time female directors closed for 2026 on February 28. Watch the grants page for the next round.

records.notes: The events page shows no current events; the newest listings are from 2024 and older, and the homepage notice about a 2025 calendar is out of date. Status active rests on the grant page's posting in September 2025 and its January 30, 2026 update, not on events. The members list is dated April 2024 and is not used as evidence of life. The join page does not restrict membership by gender. The grant award amount is not stated. Tier 1 had the site as http; the record uses https.

records.name: Piffaro, the Renaissance Band
records.summary: A Renaissance music ensemble that plays on period instruments in concerts in Philadelphia, in Wilmington, DE, and online. It also runs a free recorder class for students at one school, and it needs volunteer ushers for its concerts.
records.what_you_do: Go to a concert, usher at one for free admission, or watch for the next Recorder Fest or early music workshop on the site.

schedule.text: Concerts run through the season, and a season pass covers them. Each concert date is posted on the site.

cost.text: Each concert listing shows its ticket price, and season passes are on a separate page. Youth and full-time students with ID can get free tickets.

access.notes: All of the group's venues are wheelchair accessible. Add a note to your ticket order for wheelchair or walker friendly seating. Other access questions go to info@piffaro.org.

first_step.how: Buy a ticket for the October 16 or 17 concert through the Get Tickets link on piffaro.org/concerts, or send the usher volunteer form.
first_step.basis: Concerts are open to the public with a ticket, and ushers are recruited through a public form. No public classes or ensemble auditions are listed.
first_step.what_to_expect: The October concerts are held in churches and play Renaissance music on period instruments. Ushers arrive about 45 minutes before the performance and stay 15 to 20 minutes after it ends, and they get free admission.
first_visit_tips: Ask for wheelchair or walker friendly seats when you order your ticket.
Full-time students with ID and youth can get free tickets, so have your ID ready.
The October 16 concert is at Church of the Holy Trinity in Rittenhouse Square, and the October 17 concert is at Presbyterian Church of Chestnut Hill.
For questions the FAQ does not answer, such as late seating and refunds, email info@piffaro.org or call 215-235-8469.

records.notes: The recorder class is a free class for 4th and 5th graders at Esperanza Academy Elementary School, registered through the school, so it is not open to the public. Tier 1 had listed it as a public class. The October concert dates and the November streaming window moved out of schedule.text, and the newest one is in last_sign_of_life. The concert page gives no year; 2026 rests on the season pass wording from tier 1. Recorder Fest was March 7, 2026, so it is a past event. Early music is not a tag in the vocabulary, so instrument_lessons is the closest fit.

records.name: Queen Village Neighbors Association
records.summary: The neighborhood association for Queen Village, founded in 1969. It follows nearby zoning and building plans through a zoning committee, organizes Friends of park groups for cleanups and planting days, and publishes a quarterly newsletter.
records.what_you_do: Join a zoning meeting, help a Friends of park group with a cleanup or planting, volunteer with QV Tree Tenders, or come to a neighborhood event.

schedule.text: The zoning committee meets on Zoom in the evening. The events page lists a zoning meeting most months, usually on a Wednesday. Park cleanups and planting days are listed on the events page as they come up.

locations.label: Office
locations.address: 709 S. 5th Street, First Floor, Philadelphia, PA 19147

cost.text: Zoning meetings and park days are free. Some neighborhood events charge tickets, so check the price on the listing.

first_step.how: Sign up for the weekly newsletter on the site, then join a park cleanup or planting day from the events page.
first_step.basis: Park days and zoning meetings are listed as public, and volunteering can be as small as an hour. The site describes no newcomer program.
first_step.what_to_expect: A park day is usually two to three hours of cleanup or planting with neighbors, often run by a Friends of park group. Zoning meetings are evening calls on Zoom where the committee reviews a nearby project, and neighbors can give input.
first_visit_tips: Check the events page close to the date, since times and places are posted there.
For zoning questions, email info@qvna.org and put 'Zoning Page' in the subject line.
Park days happen at parks the Friends of groups look after, such as Weccacoe Playground, Mario Lanza Park and Bainbridge Green.
Some neighborhood events charge tickets, so check the price before you go.

records.notes: The events page lists Zoom zoning meetings from July through December 2026, and park cleanup and planting days through November. Board minutes are posted for meetings from December 2024 to June 2026, with gaps. The page gives no board meeting times or places and does not say whether board meetings are open. The site says membership counts as a donation but does not explain how to join, so no membership step is written. The volunteer sign-up form did not show on the page, so the newsletter and info@qvna.org are the routes. Zoning committee members must be Queen Village residents; the members are named on the zoning page and are not recorded here. The contact email is the City list address (sam@qvna.org). The site's general address is info@qvna.org, which appears in first_visit_tips.
